newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in slow trading on Friday with most investors staying on the sidelines ahead of the weekend, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at 3,198 yuan ($386) per tonne, losing two yuan. It opened at an intraday high of 3,200 yuan and hit a low of 3,188 yuan per tonne.
November rose three yuan to 3,167, the January 1998 contract two to 3,160 and March was unchanged at 3,150 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 23,200 tonnes from 24,100 tonnes.
Soybeans opened little changed from Thursday's close and moved around opening levels for most of the session, traders said.
"Many investors have little interest in trading because the market has been sluggish for so long," one trader said. "With the approach of the weekend, a lot of investors offset their positions."
Traders said they expected soybean activity to remain low key in the short term.
